title: Vector similarity retrieval
content: Vector similarity retrieval compares an embedding for a user query with embeddings stored for document chunks. PostgreSQL pgvector supports cosine distance, inner product, and L2 distance operators. The HNSW index accelerates approximate nearest-neighbor search. The embedding model used at indexing time must match the model used for query embeddings so vectors share the same semantic space.

title: Hybrid retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion
content: Hybrid search combines semantic vector retrieval with lexical PostgreSQL full-text search. Vector search can find semantically related passages even when wording differs, while full-text search is effective for exact terms, identifiers, and product names. Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines the two ranked candidate lists without requiring their raw scores to be calibrated to the same scale.

title: Document chunking and source offsets
content: Document chunking divides long source text into smaller passages that fit embedding and retrieval limits. A configurable overlap helps preserve context across chunk boundaries. Each chunk stores its ordinal, start character, end character, and content hash. Exact source offsets allow the retrieved excerpt to be compared with the original document during citation verification.

title: Tenant isolation for retrieval
content: Tenant-scoped retrieval must derive the tenant identifier from a verified access token and an active issuer-scoped membership. Every document and chunk query includes the tenant boundary, and PostgreSQL Row Level Security applies the same tenant identifier through a transaction-local database setting. Composite foreign keys prevent a chunk from referencing a document owned by a different tenant.

title: Citation provenance and integrity checks
content: A verifiable retrieval citation records the document identifier, chunk identifier, canonical source URI, source SHA-256, chunk SHA-256, and exact character offsets. Citation verification recomputes the source and chunk hashes and confirms that slicing the original content at the recorded offsets produces the retrieved excerpt. A citation is not considered verified when any hash or offset check fails.

title: Metadata filtering in document retrieval
content: Metadata filtering narrows retrieval to documents that match structured attributes such as department, classification, language, project, or document type. PostgreSQL JSONB containment can apply these filters before ranking candidates. The filter must be validated as a bounded JSON object and combined with the authenticated tenant predicate rather than treated as an authorization mechanism by itself.

title: Retrieval quality evaluation metrics
content: Retrieval quality should be evaluated with a versioned query set and human-reviewed relevant source labels. Recall at K measures how many relevant sources appear in the first K results. Mean Reciprocal Rank measures the position of the first relevant result. Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain rewards relevant sources appearing higher in the ranked list. Results should be reported by dataset version and embedding model.

title: Embedding ingestion and model versioning
content: Document ingestion extracts normalized text, computes a SHA-256 digest, splits the content into deterministic chunks, and requests a real embedding for every chunk. The embedding model identifier is stored with the document so retrieval does not compare vectors generated by incompatible models. Failed embedding requests must fail closed; zero vectors, random vectors, and mock responses must never be written to production retrieval storage.
